# Rules, with up to three examples each:
# rust-keeps-default-ignorables: UTS #39 internalSkeleton removes Default_Ignorable_Code_Point characters (step 2). unicode-security 0.1.2 predates that step and keeps them, so its skeleton differs wherever one occurs.
#   code point skeleton: U+00AD icu=<empty> rust=itself
#   code point skeleton: U+034F icu=<empty> rust=itself
#   code point skeleton: U+061C icu=<empty> rust=itself
# rust-lacks-hntl: UTS #39 revision 34 adds Hntl to the augmented script sets of Han and Latin characters. unicode-security 0.1.2 predates it, so its resolved script sets lack Hntl, and strings that are single-script only through Hntl (Latin with Han) get a lower restriction level.
#   resolved script set: 0061 0064 006D 0131 006E icu=Hntl Latn
#   resolved script set: FF50 FF41 FF59 FF50 FF41 FF4C icu=Hntl Latn
#   resolved script set: 01C9 0065 0074 006F icu=Hntl Latn
# rust-ignores-canonical-equivalence: UTS #39 section 3.1 applies canonical equivalence when testing for Allowed characters, so a string is in the profile if its decomposed or composed form is. unicode-security tests the characters as written, so where the two disagree it puts the string at a different restriction level.
#   restriction level: 0114 icu=SINGLE_SCRIPT rust=UNRESTRICTED
#   restriction level: 0627 0653 icu=SINGLE_SCRIPT rust=UNRESTRICTED
#   restriction level: 0044 032D icu=SINGLE_SCRIPT rust=UNRESTRICTED
# rust-unknown-is-empty: Unassigned and private-use code points have Script_Extensions {Zzzz} (Unknown), so by UTS #39 section 5.1 a string made only of them has the resolved script set {Zzzz}, as ICU computes. unicode-script represents Unknown as the empty set instead.
#   resolved script set: E000
#   resolved script set: 0378
#   resolved script set: 3B8C2 DCE4A FFFE F8FF CE5FA
